newsitem.title: UK: Bomb alerts close British highway, rail stations.
newsitem.headline: Bomb alerts close British highway, rail stations.

text.p: Suspected IRA bomb warnings brought traffic chaos to northwest England on Friday, when police were forced to close at least three railway stations and the main highway.
Police said they had received a telephoned warnings using a recognised codeword that bombs had been planted at key railway stations and on the M6 motoway.
Doncaster, Crewe and Stoke-on-Trent railway stations were evacuated and the M6 motorway closed off near the city of Manchester.

This cut off the main north/south rail lines on both the east and west sides of Britain as well as one of the two main highways linking the north and south of the country. "A local organisation received a warning at 7:10 this morning using a codeword similar to one used before," said a spokeswoman for Cheshire police, responsible for vital Crewe railway station.
She said the station and the surrounding area had been evacuated. "There is major disruption here," she said.
Last month, two bombs exploded near Wilmslow railway station in northwest England, but no-one was injured, and Semtex bombs were planted on the M6.
The Irish Republican Army, which is fighting to end Britain's rule of Northern Ireland, claimed responsibility for the attacks and threats, which paralysed northwest England.

The IRA also claimed responsibility for a bomb warning that halted the Grand National horse race earlier this month and bomb threats at London railway stations have brought chaos to the capital several times in the past few weeks.
